newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Iscor names site of 1.65 bln rand project.
newsitem.headline: Iscor names site of 1.65 bln rand project.

text.p: South African iron and steel producer Iscor Ltd said on Wednesday it had chosen the Hillview site in Empangeni, Kwazulu Natal, for a mineral separation plant and smelter of its 1.65 billion rand heavy minerals project.
This Central Processing Complex (CPC) will process the heavy minerals concentrate from mines at Hillendale near Richards Bay and ilmenite from Rooiwater in the Northern Province.
Iscor announced that its board had given the go-ahead for the project on November 4.
The project will give further impetus to the expanding range and output of Iscor's Mining Division.
"Iscor has identified the Hillview site in Empangeni as the preferred location for the mineral separation plant and smelter associated for its heavy minerals project," the company said.
The construction of the CPC is not expected to start before the last quarter of 1997 and will be commissioned in stages and is scheduled to reach full production by mid 2000.
The CPC's full output is expected to boost South Africa's total production of titanium slag by about 30 percent and generate 750 million rand in foreign exchange a year.
When in full production, the CPC will annually produce 220,000 tonnes of titanium slag, 130,000 tonnes of low manganese pig iron, 35,000 tonnes of zircon and 15,000 tonnes of rutile.

"The principal source for the CPC is electricity. The waste and atmospheric emissions from the plant will be relatively insignificant in relation to industrial plants of similar size in the Empangeni/Richards Bay area," Iscor said.
The CPC will generate 400 permanent jobs when in full production and many more will accrue during the plant's construction, Iscor said.
More than 85 percent of the materials and equipment required for the CPC will be sourced in South Africa.
Titanium slag and rutile are used to produce titanium dioxide pigment, a non-toxic and biologically inert product used in paint and paper to impart a brilliant, glossy, white colour.
Zircon is also able to scatter and reflect light and is used extensively in the ceramics industry to produce high quality glazed finishes.
